{{short description|American mathematics education researcher}}
'''Lynda R. Wiest''' is an American mathematics education researcher and professor at the [[University of Nevada, Reno]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Lynda Wiest {{!}} Equity, Diversity, and Language Education {{!}} College of Education and Human Development|url=https://www.unr.edu/education/faculty-and-staff/equity-diversity-and-language-education/lynda-wiest|access-date=2020-12-31|website=University of Nevada, Reno|language=en}}</ref>

==Research==
Wiest investigates [[mathematics education]], educational equity, and teacher education.<ref name=":0" />

==Education==
Wiest earned her B.S. degree in 1979 and her M.Ed. degree in 1984, both from [[Bloomsburg University of Pennsylvania]]. After teaching elementary and middle school students for eleven years in Pennsylvania, she earned her Ph.D. at [[Indiana University Bloomington]] in 1996. Her Ph.D. advisor was Frank Klein Lester, Jr., and her dissertation title is ''The Role of Fantasy and Real-World Problem Contexts in Fourth- and Sixth-Grade Students' Mathematical Problem Solving.''<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lynda R. Wiest|url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=119690|website=Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref>

==Career==
In 1996, Wiest joined the faculty at the University of Nevada, Reno in the College of Education. She earned tenure and was promoted to Associate Professor in 2001, and she was promoted to Professor in 2009.

In 1998, Wiest founded the Northern Nevada Girls Math and Technology Program.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Northern Nevada Math and Technology Program {{!}} College of Education and Human Development|url=https://www.unr.edu/education/centers-and-student-resources/initiatives/northern-nevada-math-technology-program|access-date=2020-12-31|website=University of Nevada, Reno|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Math Camp Application {{!}} College of Education and Human Development|url=https://www.unr.edu/education/centers-and-student-resources/initiatives/northern-nevada-math-technology-program/registration|access-date=2020-12-31|website=University of Nevada, Reno|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Service|first=LVN News|title=UNR technology program teaches computer science|url=https://www.nevadaappeal.com/news/lahontan-valley/unr-technology-program-teaches-computer-science/|access-date=2020-12-31|website=www.nevadaappeal.com|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
In 2021, Wiest received the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] (AWM) [[Louise Hay Award]] for "contribut[ing] impactfully to advancing mathematics education in K-12 across a variety of school settings. She has created innovative courses and summer programs, addressing gender equity and diversity issues."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Louise Hay Award 2021 Winner: Dr. Lynda R. Wiest|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/hay-award/hay-award-2021/|website=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Lynda R. Wiest Wins the Hay Award|work=AWM Newsletter|url=https://awm-math.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/AWM-News-JanFeb-2021-WEB.pdf}}</ref> She received the Women in Leadership STEM Award, from the Girl Scouts of the Sierra Nevada in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|author=Staff report|title=Good News: Sierra Nevada Girl Scouts honor 5 leaders|url=https://www.rgj.com/story/news/2015/11/14/good-news-sierra-nevada-girl-scouts-honor-leaders/75674596/|access-date=2020-12-31|website=Reno Gazette Journal|language=en-US}}</ref> She earned the F. Donald Tibbitts Distinguished Teacher Award from the University of Nevada, Reno in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|title=F. Donald Tibbitts Distinguished Teacher Award {{!}} Faculty Affairs {{!}} Office of the Provost and Executive Vice President|url=https://www.unr.edu/provost/faculty-affairs/recognition-and-awards/f-donald-tibbitts-distinguished-teacher-award|access-date=2020-12-31|website=University of Nevada, Reno|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=These people do it as routine practice|url=https://www.unr.edu/nevada-today/news/2015/tibbitts-award-2015|access-date=2020-12-31|website=University of Nevada, Reno|language=en}}</ref> She won the Nevada Regent’s Academic Advisor Award (graduate level) in 2003.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Regents' Academic Advisor Award {{!}} Faculty Affairs {{!}} Office of the Provost and Executive Vice President|url=https://www.unr.edu/provost/faculty-affairs/recognition-and-awards/regents-academic-advisor-award|access-date=2020-12-31|website=University of Nevada, Reno|language=en}}</ref>
